top_categories.workout_context: At mile 60 of 129, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
96ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
At Seorak GranFondo, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
12,467ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Seorak GranFondo's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 129 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
12,467ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Seorak GranFondo. Train it until it feels boring.

Road-specific control matters at Seorak GranFondo. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 129 miles.
129 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.
Low-cadence force work supports 12,467ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 12,467ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.

race_overlay.heat: June in Sangnam-myeon, Inje-gun, Gangwon-do, South Korea can bring heat. Complete 3–4 heat exposure sessions in the final 2 weeks before Seorak GranFondo. Increase sodium intake 48 hours before race day.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Seorak GranFondo’s 129 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at Seorak GranFondo. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Seorak GranFondo rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, TT Threshold, and Over Under to prepare you for 129 miles of mixed terrain in Sangnam-myeon, Inje-gun, Gangwon-do, South Korea.
